trial.title: Fetoscopic Repair of Isolated Fetal Spina Bifida

endpoints.measure: Ability to perform fetoscopic spina bifida repair
endpoints.time_frame: From time of surgery until delivery (up to 21 weeks)
endpoints.description: Successful complete closure of the defect fetoscopically and reversal of hindbrain herniation on ultrasound and MRI prior to delivery

endpoints.measure: Maternal obstetric outcome as evidenced by preterm premature rupture of membranes
endpoints.time_frame: From time of surgery until 37 weeks of gestation (up to 18 weeks)
endpoints.description: Preterm premature rupture of membranes occuring any time from surgery until 37 weeks of gestation

endpoints.measure: Maternal obstetric outcome as evidenced by preterm labor leading to delivery at less than 34 weeks of gestation
endpoints.time_frame: From time of surgery until 34 weeks of gestation (up to 15 weeks)
endpoints.description: Preterm labor occuring at any time from surgery leading to delivery before 34 weeks of gestation

endpoints.measure: Maternal obstetric outcome as evidenced by gestational age at delivery
endpoints.time_frame: From time of surgery until delivery (up to 21 weeks)
endpoints.description: Gestational age of delivery regardless of indication

endpoints.measure: Maternal obstetric outcome as evidenced by the ability to delivery vaginally
endpoints.time_frame: From time of surgery until delivery (up to 21 weeks)
endpoints.description: Mode of delivery - either vaginal or cesarean section

endpoints.measure: Adverse fetal or neonatal outcome as evidenced by fetal or neonatal death
endpoints.time_frame: From the time of surgery until 28 days of life (up 25 weeks)
endpoints.description: Composite of fetal or neonatal death

endpoints.measure: Adverse early childhood outcome as evidenced by need for a cerebrospinal fluid shunt
endpoints.time_frame: From the time of birth until 12 months of life
endpoints.description: Need for a cerebrospinal fluid shunt within the first year of life

endpoints.measure: Neurodevelopmental outcome as evaluated by the Bayley Scales of Infant Development II
endpoints.description: Score of the Mental Developmental Index of the Bayley Scales of Infant Development II at 30 months of age. The score ranges from 50 (minimum) to 150 (maximum). A score of \<70 indicates severe developmental delay; 70-84 indicates moderate delay; \>85 indicates no delay.

endpoints.measure: Early childhood motor function on physical examination
endpoints.description: Difference between the anatomic upper border of the lesion level and motor function based on the physical examination at 30 months of age. A positive score of 2 indicates a functional level 2 vertebrae higher than lesion level. A score of -2 indicates a function level 2 vertebrae lower than the lesion level.

outcome.rationale: Fetoscopic repair is technically feasible with high success rate for defect closure and hindbrain reversal. Primary endpoint likely to be met. However, high PPROM and preterm delivery rates remain significant challenges. Neurodevelopmental outcomes appear comparable to open fetal surgery.

value.estimand: single_arm proportion successful fetoscopic repair with defect closure and hindbrain reversal
value.uncertainty: Laparotomy-assisted technique may differ from reported percutaneous outcomes; limited direct evidence for this specific approach
value.rationale: Based on Gielchinsky 2026 showing 95% procedure completion with hindbrain reversal in percutaneous approach. Laparotomy-assisted approach may have similar or better technical success. Predict 92% success rate.

value.estimand: proportion with PPROM from surgery to 37 weeks
value.uncertainty: Laparotomy-assisted approach may have lower PPROM than totally percutaneous (68% reported); limited comparative data
value.rationale: Gielchinsky 2026 reported 68% PPROM with percutaneous approach. Laparotomy-assisted technique may reduce membrane trauma, but PPROM remains common. Predict 65% incidence.

value.uncertainty: Median delivery 32.7 weeks in percutaneous series suggests substantial preterm delivery; laparotomy approach may differ
value.rationale: Median gestational age at delivery 32.7 weeks in percutaneous series. Approximately 50% deliver before 34 weeks. Predict 45% preterm delivery <34 weeks for laparotomy-assisted approach.

value.estimand: mean gestational age at delivery in weeks
value.uncertainty: Limited data on laparotomy-assisted approach; percutaneous series showed median 32.7 weeks
value.rationale: Based on median 32.7 weeks in percutaneous series. Laparotomy-assisted approach may allow slightly longer gestation. Predict mean 33.5 weeks.

value.uncertainty: Vaginal delivery after laparotomy-assisted approach feasible but depends on surgical technique and obstetric management
value.rationale: Gielchinsky 2026 reported 50% vaginal delivery with percutaneous approach. Laparotomy-assisted approach preserves uterine integrity similarly. Predict 50% vaginal delivery rate.

value.estimand: proportion fetal or neonatal death by 28 days
value.uncertainty: No neonatal deaths reported in Gielchinsky series; mortality risk exists with preterm delivery but overall low in experienced centers
value.rationale: Gielchinsky 2026 reported no neonatal deaths in 22 cases. Perinatal mortality in experienced centers is low. Predict 5% mortality accounting for preterm delivery risks.

value.estimand: proportion requiring CSF shunt by 12 months
value.uncertainty: Gielchinsky reported 31.8% shunt rate; Lapa reported 46.6% shunt rate (53.4% no shunt). Range 30-50% likely.
value.rationale: Gielchinsky 2026: 31.8% shunt rate. Lapa 2021: 46.6% shunt rate. Laparotomy-assisted approach may be similar to percutaneous. Predict 35% shunt requirement.

value.estimand: mean Bayley MDI score at 30 months
value.uncertainty: Limited 30-month follow-up data; Lapa series showed functional outcomes but not specific Bayley scores
value.rationale: No direct Bayley score data from fetoscopic series. Lapa 2021 showed 54% independent ambulation at 30 months suggesting reasonable neurodevelopment. Predict mean MDI ~85 (borderline normal).

value.estimand: proportion with motor improvement ≥2 levels at 30 months
value.uncertainty: Gielchinsky reported 68% with ≥2 level improvement; laparotomy-assisted approach may have similar functional outcomes
value.rationale: Gielchinsky 2026 reported 68% motor improvement ≥2 levels with percutaneous approach. Laparotomy-assisted approach should achieve similar neurological benefits. Predict 68% improvement rate.

analysis_trace: Trial NCT03090633 is a single-arm study of fetoscopic repair of isolated fetal spina bifida (myelomeningocele) using laparotomy with uterine exteriorization. The study enrolled 30 patients with gestational age 19-25 weeks and lesion levels T1-S1.

Evidence from retrieved sources: Gielchinsky et al. 2026 (PMID 42278950, PMC13258459) reported on 22 fetuses undergoing totally percutaneous fetoscopic repair using SAFER technique. Procedure completion rate was 95%, PPROM occurred in 68%, median gestational age at delivery was 32.7 weeks, vaginal delivery achieved in 50%, CSF diversion rate 31.8%, hindbrain herniation reversal in 95%, motor improvement ≥2 levels in 68%.

Lapa et al. 2021 (PMID 33880811, PMC9293198) reported on 170 patients across 8 centers using percutaneous fetoscopic SAFER technique. At 12 months, 53.4% did not require CSF diversion; at 30 months, 54.2% ambulated independently and 61% did not require bladder catheterization.

Key differences: NCT03090633 uses laparotomy-assisted approach (not totally percutaneous), which may have different risk profiles. The laparotomy-assisted approach may reduce PPROM rates compared to percutaneous approach but increases maternal surgical morbidity.

Evidence-role assignments: PMC13258459 supports primary-0 (indirect_direction, procedure completion 95%), secondary-0 (direct_numeric, PPROM 68%), secondary-1 (indirect_direction, preterm delivery common), secondary-2 (direct_numeric, median delivery 32.7 weeks), secondary-3 (direct_numeric, vaginal delivery 50%), secondary-5 (direct_numeric, CSF diversion 31.8%), secondary-7 (direct_numeric, motor improvement 68%). PMC9293198 supports secondary-5 (indirect_direction, no-shunt rate 53.4%) and secondary-6/secondary-7 (indirect_direction, functional outcomes).

Uncertainty: Laparotomy-assisted vs percutaneous technique differences; single-center experience; small sample size (n=30 estimated); long-term neurodevelopmental outcomes at 30 months have limited follow-up data.
Safety considerations: PPROM and preterm delivery are major obstetric risks. Fetal/neonatal death risk exists but appears low based on published series. No maternal deaths reported in similar series.

Trial outcome prediction: The trial is likely to demonstrate feasibility of fetoscopic repair with successful defect closure and hindbrain reversal in majority of cases, but high PPROM and preterm delivery rates are expected. Primary endpoint (technical success) likely to be met in >90% of cases.
